claims.claim: IBM reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.2 billion, up 1 percent.
GAAP pre-tax income was down 5 percent year over year.
Management raised its full-year constant-currency revenue growth expectation to four-to-five percent.
claims.note: The release says the company 'now expects' four-to-five percent and 'provides updated full-year expectations', but never gives the prior range. The direction of the revision (raised versus lowered) cannot be established from the release and requires outside knowledge.

claims.claim: Revenue was $17,162 million.
Gross profit was $9.9 billion.
Gross profit margin was 57.7 percent, down 1.0 points year over year.
GAAP pre-tax income was $2.5 billion.
GAAP pre-tax margin was 14.4 percent, down 0.9 points.
Net income was $2.2 billion, down 1 percent.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $2.27, versus $2.31 in the prior-year quarter.
Operating (non-GAAP) gross profit was $10.2 billion at a 59.4 percent margin.
Operating (non-GAAP) pre-tax income was $3.3 billion, up 3 percent, at a 19.2 percent margin, up 0.3 points.
Operating (non-GAAP) net income was $2.8 billion, up 5 percent.
Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.93, up 5 percent.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $4.8 billion with a 27.8 percent margin, up 0.2 points.
GAAP effective tax rate was 12.6 percent versus 15.5 percent a year ago.
Operating (non-GAAP) effective tax rate was 15.1 percent versus 17.0 percent.
R&D expense was $2,311 million versus $2,097 million.
SG&A was $4,981 million versus $5,027 million.
Software revenue was $7.8 billion, up 5 percent.
Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) was up 11 percent.
Data was up 19 percent, up 18 percent at constant currency.
Automation was up 4 percent, up 3 percent at constant currency.
Transaction Processing was down 8 percent, down 9 percent at constant currency.
Software segment profit margin was 32.2 percent versus 31.1 percent.
Consulting revenue was $5.3 billion, flat, up 1 percent at constant currency.
Strategy and Technology and Intelligent Operations were both flat, up 1 percent at constant currency.
Consulting segment profit margin was 12.1 percent versus 10.6 percent.
Infrastructure revenue was $3.8 billion, down 7 percent.
Hybrid Infrastructure was down 10 percent, with IBM Z down 42 percent and Distributed Infrastructure up 37 percent.
Infrastructure Support was down 1 percent.
Infrastructure segment profit margin was 21.8 percent versus 23.3 percent.
The release says Power and Storage grew at a record pace, with an order backlog of nearly $500 million.
Financing revenue was $0.2 billion, up 12 percent, up 11 percent at constant currency.
The CFO cited 'revenue headwinds late in the second quarter'.
For full-year 2026 the company now expects constant-currency revenue growth of four-to-five percent.
At current FX rates, currency is expected to be neutral to growth for the year.
The company continues to expect full-year 2026 free cash flow (non-GAAP) to increase by about $1 billion year over year.
The company now expects improved pre-tax income margin expansion for the full year.
Second-quarter net cash from operating activities was $2.6 billion, up $0.9 billion year to year.
Second-quarter free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $2.5 billion, down $0.3 billion.
For the first six months, operating cash flow was $7.8 billion, up $1.7 billion.
For the first six months, free cash flow was $4.8 billion, flat year to year.
IBM ended the quarter with $8.2 billion of cash, restricted cash and marketable securities, down $6.3 billion from year-end 2025.
IBM invested $10.5 billion in acquisitions this year.
Debt totaled $62.0 billion, including $13.0 billion of IBM Financing debt, up $0.7 billion year to date.
IBM returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in dividends in the second quarter.
IBM declared a quarterly dividend of $1.69 per share, record date August 10, payable September 10, 2026.
IBM Z fell 42 percent while Distributed Infrastructure rose 37 percent.
The Power/Storage order backlog is nearly $500 million.
The CFO referenced unspecified 'revenue headwinds late in the second quarter'.
The constant-currency growth range was raised.
claims.note: Repeat of the lede error in the watch items. The release discloses only the current four-to-five percent range, not the prior one, so it does not support characterizing the range as raised.

claims.claim: Cash fell $6.3 billion from year-end after $10.5 billion of acquisitions.
Second-quarter free cash flow declined $0.3 billion.
The company targets a full-year free cash flow increase of about $1 billion.
The GAAP effective tax rate of 12.6 percent was lower than the prior-year rate.
